title: go sdk: stream read timeouts, backpressure signaling and graceful-close semantics
creator: Riya Patel
description:
Background: Customers building high-throughput LLM features report two recurring issues with the Go SDK streaming API: 1) ambiguous timeout semantics where application-level deadlines mingle with transport read deadlines, leading either to unexpected cancellations or to long waits; 2) lack of a consistent signal for backpressure and graceful stream shutdown which complicates reconnect and retry logic for client applications and platform-level racks (Dedicated/Private).

Goal: Deliver clear, ergonomic primitives in the Go SDK to: (a) separate operation deadlines from transport idle timeouts; (b) provide explicit backpressure and graceful-close signals so callers can decide whether to reconnect, retry at a higher level, or fail fast; (c) make common cancellation patterns (context deadlines, SIGINT, and parent stream closure) easy and consistent; (d) include well-documented examples and tests to show recommended usage patterns for production services.

Scope: API additions and behavior changes for the Go SDK streaming client only (no server/runtime changes). Backwards-compatible where possible; provide migration notes for existing users. Acceptance tests must cover deadline propagation, reconnect with jittered exponential backoff, and graceful shutdown drains.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce StreamOptions with distinct IdleTimeout (transport idle) and OperationDeadline (logical op) fields and document precedence rules.
Expose ReadLoop(ctx) helper that returns typed CloseReason and error so callers can differentiate app cancellation vs network EOF vs server-initiated graceful close.
Emit BackpressureSignal() callback that application code can use to temporarily throttle request production and surface metrics (SDK exposes counters/metrics hooks).
Reconnect behavior implemented in example client: exponential backoff with full jitter, configurable maxRetries, and per-attempt OperationDeadline reset rules.
Comprehensive unit + integration tests covering: context deadline triggers, OS signal-based cancellation (SIGTERM), forced transport timeouts, and successful graceful-close handshake.
Documentation and example code added to docs/sdk/go/streaming.md and a migration snippet for existing users; deprecation notes if any breaking behavior exists.
Performance regression: no more than 2% added latency for streaming happy-path in CI microbenchmarks after changes.
technical_notes: API: Add type StreamOptions struct { IdleTimeout string; OperationDeadline string; BackpressureThreshold int; EnableReconnect bool; MaxReconnectAttempts int } - string durations to keep JSON-friendly config parsing; SDK will parse with time.ParseDuration.

API: Add func (s *Stream) ReadLoop(ctx context.Context) (CloseReason string, err error). CloseReason values: "app_canceled", "context_deadline", "transport_eof", "server_graceful_close", "network_error".

Backpressure: SDK will call user-provided BackpressureCallback(percentFull int) when local send queue crosses thresholds. Example will show a simple token-bucket producer that pauses on callback until drained.

Timeout semantics: OperationDeadline is applied to high-level request life (e.g., overall generation); IdleTimeout is applied to transport-level read inactivity (no new token frames). If OperationDeadline expires, SDK returns context_deadline; if IdleTimeout fires, SDK returns network_error with metric tags for 'idle_timeout'.

Reconnect: examples will show knobging rules - OperationDeadline is not automatically extended on reconnect attempts; callers must choose to restart operation or continue. We will provide a helper RetryWithReconnect(ctx, opts, connectFn, streamHandler) that implements exponential backoff with full jitter and honors an overall caller context.

Migration: default behavior remains the same unless user passes StreamOptions. We will document corner cases where previously a read could block indefinitely and now will be subject to IdleTimeout default (30s).
Metrics: export sdk_stream_read_timeouts_total, sdk_stream_graceful_closes_total, sdk_stream_reconnects_total, sdk_stream_backpressure_events_total with tags for model and route.
Testing: new integration harness will run with a fake server that simulates server_graceful_close and transport stalls to validate CloseReason values and reconnect helper behavior.

Implementation note: avoid changing existing exported types; add new methods so older callers still compile. Use feature-flagged defaults to enable new semantics for internal dogfooding before public release.
decisions: Use two-tier timeout model (OperationDeadline vs IdleTimeout) instead of overloading context.Context for clarity.
Return a typed CloseReason string rather than adding multiple error types to simplify cross-language parity and SDK metrics tagging.
Expose backpressure as a callback rather than try-to-block-producer inside SDK to avoid surprising concurrency behavior for callers.
Provide a high-level RetryWithReconnect helper as an opt-in convenience; do not make it the default automatic behavior to avoid implicit retries causing duplicate downstream effects.
Default IdleTimeout = "30s" and OperationDeadline unset by default (caller must set for strict SLAs).

2026-02-24 Marcus Chen: Prototype of StreamOptions parser pushed to branch feat/stream-timeouts. Initial tests for IdleTimeout firing against net.Pipe show expected behavior. (github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/2412)

2026-03-02 Jamie Li: Integration harness skeleton added to infra/testbeds to simulate server_graceful_close frames. Found edge-case where server sends graceful_close but also a final data packet; agreed to treat server final packet as success then close.
2026-03-05 SRE (Avery Collins): Added metrics name proposals and tagging schema. Need to ensure tags include customer_id anonymized hash for billing heatmaps.
2026-03-09 Marcus Chen: Implemented ReadLoop and CloseReason enum strings. WIP: backpressure callback wiring. Manual testing shows SIGTERM cancellation maps to app_canceled CloseReason.

2026-03-11 QA (Matt Simmons): Ran unit tests against prototype. Observed intermittent flakiness when IdleTimeout=1s in CI; increased default IdleTimeout to 30s and added jitter to internal timers to reduce false positives.
